function: Learned (MADDPG) joint control of UAV trajectory, AN jamming and device transmit power, analog beamforming, bandwidth, CPU frequency and local accuracy for covert FL uplinks (pp. 8-9).
system: Full-duplex UAV (ULA) aggregates 10 multi-antenna devices; 4 single-antenna wardens; antenna configurations 4, 16, 64; mmWave Saleh-Valenzuela links; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3-4, 10).
method: MADDPG (centralized training, distributed execution): actor-critic agents per device and UAV, shared reward equal to the negative training cost; reinforcement learning, trained over episodes (pp. 8-10).
data_channel: Simulated clustered Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channels (LoS), Rayleigh fading, Rician self-interference; no standard channel model or public dataset; random 180 m x 180 m layout (pp. 4-5, 10).
test_conditions: Each setting (4, 16 or 64 antennas, security level, accuracy) has its own training curve over 2500 episodes; no separately tested unseen condition stated (pp. 10-12).
baselines: GA and PSO (non-learned); DDPG and multi-agent DQN (learned); fixed-variable Schemes 1-4 of Table II (Fig. 5) (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Training cost (latency plus weighted energy) over episodes, versus security level, global accuracy and number of antennas (pp. 7, 11-12, Figs. 3-7).
complexity: Order of complexity of the MADDPG algorithm: O(EI(Q+1)(1+I+(1+1/S)ID'+ID'')), with E episodes, I steps, Q devices, S minibatch, D', D'' data sizes (p. 10).
openness: None: no code or data link; training uses "simulated environments derived from real-world network datasets" with no dataset named (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "We utilize the commonly-used clustered Saleh-Valenzuela channel model [24], [25]"; a textbook simulator with Rayleigh fading and a Rician self-interference link, and no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "Fig. 7 illustrates the adaptability of various algorithms to security constraints"; this is a sweep of the security level, each setting in Figs. 3-4 has its own training curve, and the paper never states that a trained model is tested on an unseen scenario or antenna number.
q3_support: p. 12: "compared with genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), multi-agent deep Q-network (MADQN) algorithm and deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm"; GA and PSO are non-learned, MADQN and DDPG are standard learning algorithms on the same problem, compared on the training cost (Figs. 6-7).
q4_support: p. 10: "the computational complexity is in the order of O(EI(Q + 1)" followed by the full expression for Algorithm 1.
q5_support: p. 10: "utilizing simulated environments derived from real-world network datasets"; no dataset is named, no link or DOI is given, no code release is stated, and the channels are simulated (p. 4).
notes: Included under area 6: the MADDPG agents control transmit and jamming power, analog beamforming vectors and bandwidth on an air-to-ground link (action vectors on pp. 8-9, eqs. 58-59), jointly with UAV trajectory, CPU frequency and local accuracy, so a physical-layer decision is learned jointly with one above it and the above_phy exclusion does not apply. Area 7 does not apply: the UAV averages the received local updates digitally (p. 4, eq. 8) and the upload latency follows from a per-device rate (p. 5), with no over-the-air computation; AirComp appears only in the related work (p. 2). Covert communication is not in the list of excluded functions, but the reviewer may wish to confirm that area 6 (power and beam control of an aerial link) is the right reading, since the objective is the FL training cost under covertness constraints. q3 counts GA, PSO, MADQN and DDPG; Schemes 1-4 of Table II (fixed variables of the proposed method) are variants and are not counted. The sentence on p. 10 about real-world network datasets names no dataset, so q1 and q5 stay 0.
